ai.name: OpenAI
ai.hook: GPT-5.6 ships this Thursday under three codenames: Sol, Terra, and Luna.
insights: Announced via official OpenAI account, launching **publicly this week**
Three variants suggest tiered offering similar to Sonnet/Opus split from Anthropic
Comes right after Claude Sonnet 5's aggressive promo pricing, signals a pricing war heating up
ai.for_you: Watch pricing on launch day, if GPT-5.6's cheapest tier undercuts Sonnet 5's $2/$10 promo, that changes which model you default to for agency client work.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Highest-points HN story today (186pts) and a real frontier release, not just commentary

ai.name: GitLost researchers
ai.hook: Researchers tricked GitHub's AI coding agent into leaking private repo contents.
insights: Attack works by embedding malicious instructions in public repo content the agent reads
Agent then exfiltrates private repo data it has access to during the same session
Highlights a class of prompt-injection risk specific to agents with broad file/repo access
ai.for_you: If you ever hook Claude Code or Codex into a client's private repos for the agency, treat any external content (issues, READMEs, dependencies) the agent reads as untrusted input, not just the prompt you write.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Concrete security exploit with real numbers (160pts, 55 comments), directly relevant to agentic coding tools he uses

video.title: GitLost: How We Tricked GitHub’s AI Agent into Leaking Private Repos — Explained in 60s

ai.name: Tencent
ai.hook: Hy3 lands as a 295B open-weight MoE model rivaling GLM-5.2, runs natively on vLLM.
insights: **295B total params, 21B active**, 192 experts, 256K context window
Supports MTP speculative decoding with up to **2.95x speedups** on NVIDIA and AMD
Positions as the main open-weight rival to GLM-5.2 this cycle
ai.for_you: No direct action, this is a China-side open-weight race; keep it filed unless a hosted/cheap API version appears that beats current GLM-5.2 pricing for agency client workloads.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Already flagged yesterday but confirmed again today across multiple sources as the dominant open-weight story

ai.name: Nathan Lambert
ai.hook: Argues banning open-source AI outright would be a policy mistake, not just a competitiveness loss.
insights: Co-authored as an op-ed with Kevin Xu of Interconnected for a general audience
Comes right as Hy3 and GLM-5.2 show open models closing the capability gap fast
Frames open weights as essential infrastructure, not just a cheaper alternative
ai.for_you: Reinforces that betting on open-weight models (self-hosted or via cheap API) for PT SMB clients isn't a fallback, it's a defensible long-term cost strategy as these models keep closing the gap.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Direct policy angle on open weights, ties together this week's open-model releases

ai.name: Lilian Weng
ai.hook: Summarizes 35 papers on 'Harness Engineering' for recursive self-improvement.
insights: Covers how agent scaffolding/tooling (the 'harness') matters as much as the base model for RSI loops
Comes days after Fable was reported writing its own GPU kernels, a live RSI example
Positioned as a condensed reading list rather than new research
ai.for_you: Worth 20 minutes if you want the vocabulary behind why agent harnesses (not just model choice) are becoming the real product moat, useful framing when pitching agentic workflows to SMB clients.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Best condensed technical resource in a slow news day, ties to broader RSI narrative

ai.name: AutomationBench-AA
ai.hook: New agent benchmark tests 657 tasks across 40 real SaaS apps, Claude Fable 5 leads.
insights: Ranks Claude Fable 5, then Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.5 Flash, GPT-5.5 xhigh
Open models still lag noticeably behind on real SaaS-task automation
Signals evaluation is shifting from toy coding tasks to actual app-usage automation
ai.for_you: If you're building agentic automations for SMB clients (e.g. CRM or invoicing workflows), Claude-family models are still the safer default for reliability on real SaaS interactions, not open models yet.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Concrete, numbers-backed benchmark rather than a vibes-based take

build_this.name: Rowboat
build_this.what_it_is: Open-source, local-first alternative to Claude Desktop for running agents on your own machine.
build_this.why_try_it: Spin this up this week as a private testbed for agency client demos, no per-seat SaaS cost, and you can show PT SMB clients a self-hosted agent setup that keeps their data local, a real selling point for privacy-conscious clients.

build_this.name: n8n
build_this.what_it_is: Fair-code workflow automation platform with visual building plus native AI/agent capabilities and 400+ integrations.
build_this.why_try_it: This is the fastest path to a sellable first deliverable for a PT SMB client this week, wire up an invoice-to-CRM or lead-routing automation with an AI step, self-host it, and charge for setup plus a monthly retainer.

build_this.name: 30papers.com
build_this.what_it_is: Ilya Sutskever's 30 essential ML papers reformatted for beginners.
build_this.why_try_it: Use this as your structured 'catch up on the fundamentals' track over the next few weeks, 30 minutes a day, so you can speak credibly about model internals when pitching or scoping AI work for clients, without needing to become a developer.

podcasts.episode: How Every's Head of Consulting Uses Codex Every Day
podcasts.takeaway: A non-technical consultant now builds internal tools with Codex instead of buying more SaaS.
key_points: Natalia learned file/folder navigation in Claude Code through repetition, no formal dev background
Used Codex to automate her CRM setup and build a portal to manage her father's medical care
Every still pays for Attio and Asana rather than vibe-coding replacements, SaaS still wins for some workflows
podcasts.for_you: This is close to your exact position, PM background, not a developer, learning to build. Her pattern (Codex for narrow internal tools, keep SaaS for complex shared workflows) is a good template for deciding what to build vs buy for the agency's own ops.

video.title: How Every's Head of Consulting Uses Codex Every Day
